author: CONTRIBUTED REPORT
title: Prescribed burns set for fall - NewsBreak
text: BIG PINE KEY — The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service plans to conduct prescribed burns in one or more locations within the National Key Deer Refuge between September and December. When suitable weather conditions are presented, professional fire specialists will implement the prescribed burns. The primary reasons for the burns are to remove the over accumulation of vegetation acting as fire fuel where wildlands and homes meet to protect community private property and residents, and for ecological purposes aimed at mimicking a natural fire in the pine rockland habitat. This activity creates a space between refuge lands and private property that helps to prevent or reduce the threat of wildfires by reducing fuel loads, according to FWS. Restoration and maintenance of the fire-dependent pine rockland habitat is essential for a healthy ecosystem. Prescribed burns are important for the continued survival of local species such as the federally endangered Key deer, the Bartram’s hairstreak butterfly and the butterfly’s host plant, pineland croton, which has evolved to be dependent upon fire. Mechanized methods have also been used to strengthen fire breaks, as well as to mimic fire and restore pineland croton habitat in areas that are too overgrown or too close to private property to safely conduct prescribed fire activities. To be added to the refuge’s Smoke Sensitive Contact List, send an email to keydeer@fws.gov with the subject line “Add me to the Smoke Sensitive Contact List” with name and phone number in the email, or call 305-872-0774 and ask to be added to the Smoke Sensitive Contact List with name and phone number. For updates, visit the refuge's Facebook page at facebook.com/floridakeysrefuges or contact Public Information Officer Erin Myers at 239-370-6302 or erin_myers@fws.gov.
